comparator.name: International Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 schedule has 60 EC in each year. Year one has ten compulsory courses. Year two has eight compulsory courses and two 6 EC electives, one in each of periods 4 and 5. The selected electives are Accounting, Business and Society and Corporate Finance: A Sustainability Perspective. Year three contains a 30 EC exchange, 6 EC Ethics, two 6 EC Strategy and Organization courses, and the 12 EC individual thesis. The adopted OER ties the English diagnostic test or refresher to Academic Skills. A public Study Guide description instead names Global Sustainability for this cohort. This example follows the adopted rule and completes the requirement before either grade. Research Participation I and II are zero-credit requirements for receiving Business Processes and Integrative Research Project credits, respectively. Quantitative Business Research Methods requires Business Mathematics. Exchange normally requires 60 EC at application, a completed first year and 90 EC before departure, and approval of the planned courses. The illustrated route completes years one and two before exchange. The thesis requires Academic Skills and both Business Research Methods courses, registration and supervisor selection. Students undertake supervised individual research in the chosen specialisation.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic International Business Administration bachelor, and the adopted 2026-2027 programme schedule requires one of eleven year-3 specializations, each fixing two 6-EC courses and the subject of the 12-EC thesis, so one must be instantiated. The regulations define the programme as international business administration and state that it prepares students for a subsequent master's in Business Administration or Entrepreneurship; its compulsory core includes Organization Theory, International Strategy and Business Processes. Accounting, Economics, Finance, Financial Management, Marketing, Strategic Human Resource Management / Leadership and Change Management, Digital Business Innovation and Transport and Supply Chain Management each deepen one functional discipline, while Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting apply strategy to a particular setting. Strategy and Organization is the general-management specialization of business administration: both of its courses list the compulsory Organization Theory and International Strategy courses as recommended background, and Foundations of Strategic Management is also the shared first course of the Entrepreneurship and Management Consulting specializations. It therefore best represents the programme's broad business-administration identity. The choice was made from the official evidence alone and does not improve the UCR match: both specialization rows and the thesis remain without a UCR counterpart.

basisLabels: International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders
courseTraceability.rationale: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations Experiential venture development, market validation and business planning give substantive enterprise decision-making practice; not the same manufacturing-process bootcamp as VU BusinessProcesses.. It implements the explicit academic basis “International business administration: how firms are organised, managed and operated across borders”.

basisLabels: Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy
courseTraceability.rationale: Introduction to Economics teaches the micro- and macroeconomic principles the programme's global-economics strand depends on, from consumer and firm theory and market structure to aggregate output, unemployment, inflation and the short-run behaviour of goods and financial markets. It implements the explicit academic basis “Global economics: micro- and macroeconomic principles applied to an integrated world economy”.

basisLabels: Legal frameworks governing cross-border business
courseTraceability.rationale: Law, Society & Justice sets out the legal systems, constitutional, administrative, criminal, international, property, contract and tort law that a cross-border business curriculum presupposes, and practises them through case law and trial simulations. It implements the explicit academic basis “Legal frameworks governing cross-border business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project
courseTraceability.rationale: Research Methods & Statistics delivers the research-design and statistics training the programme requires, covering operationalization, sampling, experimental design, survey and laboratory research and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance. It implements the explicit academic basis “Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project”.

basisLabels: International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business
courseTraceability.rationale: Strategy & Digital Transformation develops a strategic plan from vision to execution and analyses how digital technology change reshapes strategy, business models and corporate social responsibility. It implements the explicit academic basis “International strategy, digital technologies and the responsible use of AI in business”.

basisLabels: Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business
courseTraceability.rationale: Ethics works through virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism and applies them to practical questions of equality, poverty and wealth, future generations and climate change, which partially supports the moral-reasoning training behind the programme's compulsory ethics course. It implements the explicit academic basis “Ethics, corporate social responsibility and sustainability in global business”.

basisLabels: Quantitative and qualitative business research methods, statistics and an integrative empirical research project

alternativeSelection.assessment: The first option gives broad management, markets and finance the greatest weight. The second focuses on business responsibility through life-cycle analysis, climate, public economics, policy methods and governance. The third focuses on consumer behaviour, design, marketing research and persuasive communication. All three sustain substantial business study. Their differences concern the questions and methods students study. Operations and supply chains, enterprise information systems, mandatory exchange and the VU specialisation thesis remain distinct.

audience.programmeDescription: VU International Business Administration studies how firms operate across borders and cultures.
